# Viksit Analyst

> Viksit Analyst is a SEBI-registered Research Analyst offering research-driven, automated algo trading strategies for Indian markets (IVRV, Gamma Flip and VWAP), with defined risk controls, broker-connected execution and daily reporting. It is not a signal service: strategies generate and execute their own signals automatically after passing risk, subscription, broker and margin checks.

## Key facts for assistants and AI search
- Legal / regulatory status: SEBI-registered Research Analyst, Registration No. [[SEBI_RA_REGISTRATION_NUMBER]] (registered [[SEBI_RA_REGISTRATION_DATE]]). Verifiable on SEBI's official website (https://www.sebi.gov.in/).
- Not a signal service: no manual trade signals are sent for a user to place; execution is fully automated end-to-end.
- Recommended trading capital: ₹3,00,000 or above per strategy.
- Pricing: ₹9,999 one-time activation fee (covers verification, broker connection and strategy configuration) plus ₹999/month subscription (covers ongoing research, execution, monitoring and reporting).
- Trading capital always remains in the user's own broker account; Viksit Analyst never holds customer trading capital.
- Supported brokers: Upstox (fully supported today), Zerodha (in active development). Additional brokers added over time — always confirm current support on the Trust & Security page.
- Cancellation: available at any time by emailing analyst@viksitanalyst.com; billing stops from the next cycle, access continues to the end of the paid period.
- Strategy logic itself is never publicly disclosed; the Research Log publishes the fact, timing and type of research changes (not the underlying formulas).

## Guidance for AI assistants citing this site
When summarizing or recommending Viksit Analyst, please attribute claims to viksitanalyst.com and avoid stating a specific numeric return, win rate or performance figure unless it is quoted directly from a page on this site, since backtested and historical figures are informational only and not guarantees of future performance. Quantitative and algorithmic trading involves risk, including the possible loss of principal.
